questions.question: Q1 With 16 nodes, 500 MB gradient, and 400 Gbps (50 GB/s) injection speed, what is the theoretical RDMA sync latency?
Q2 How does TCP/IP overhead scale with the number of nodes?

answers.d: It is not affected by node count

explanations.b: Correct. TCP adds N × T_kernel overhead, scaling linearly.

questions.question: Q3 If a straggler node takes 3x longer than normal, what happens to all-reduce?

answers.b: All nodes must wait, increasing total sync time

explanations.a: Incorrect. Synchronous all-reduce requires all nodes.
explanations.b: Correct. In synchronous training, all nodes must complete before aggregation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Automatic removal requires special handling.

questions.question: Q4 What is the primary advantage of RDMA over TCP/IP for gradient synchronization?

answers.b: Zero kernel copy overhead and lower latency

explanations.a: Incorrect. Both can use the same physical bandwidth.
explanations.b: Correct. RDMA eliminates CPU/kernel overhead for direct memory transfers.
explanations.c: Incorrect. RDMA does not compress data.
explanations.d: Incorrect. RDMA configuration is typically more complex.

questions.question: Q5 As gradient tensor size doubles, theoretical sync latency:

explanations.c: Correct. Sync latency is linearly proportional to gradient size.

questions.question: Q6 What cluster compute efficiency indicates the best performance?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 10% means most time is wasted on sync.
explanations.b: Incorrect. 50% means half the time is sync overhead.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 75% is acceptable but not optimal.
explanations.d: Correct. 95% means almost all time is spent on useful computation.

questions.question: Q7 In ring all-reduce, what is the factor 2(N-1)/N approximately equal to for large N?
Q8 What happens to cluster efficiency when switching from TCP/IP to RDMA?

answers.b: It significantly increases due to reduced sync overhead

explanations.b: Correct. Lower sync latency means more time for computation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The protocol significantly affects performance.

questions.question: Q9 Which real-world application relies heavily on efficient all-reduce operations?

explanations.b: Correct. Distributed training synchronizes gradients via all-reduce after every training step.

questions.question: Q10 What is the key engineering lesson from this experiment?

answers.a: Network protocols have no impact on training performance
answers.b: RDMA provides critical performance advantages for distributed AI training by eliminating kernel overhead
answers.c: TCP/IP is always faster than RDMA
answers.d: Gradient size does not affect synchronization time

explanations.a: Incorrect. Protocol choice dramatically affects performance.
explanations.b: Correct. The experiment demonstrates the importance of hardware-offloaded networking.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Larger gradients increase sync time.
